grh_78ccfbb5c9ad8da3d6b6.title: The Neediest Case
paragraphs: When Dr. Christian finds reclusive Ivy Fenner freezing and hungry in an unheated house, he treats her as Rivers End's neediest case and organizes food, fuel, blankets, medical care and small comforts she cannot afford. Ivy remains prickly and suspicious, especially whenever anyone goes near her old mattress. After her sudden death, the reason becomes clear: ten thousand dollars has been hidden inside it, making the supposed pauper a secret miser. At first the money appears destined for the state because she left no known will, until the telephone men produce a note Ivy wrote and had them witness when they installed her phone. It leaves her estate to the only good friend she believed she had, Dr. Paul Christian, giving him the chance to turn her hoarded money toward helping others.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on January 3, 1939. It is listed as episode 37 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Gloria Holden, Josephine Hull, Frank Butler, and Berry Kroeger. Other credited names include Andre Baruch as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_78e75edaf4293c493025.title: Last Resort
paragraphs: Struggling comedian Benny Milton signs with the mysterious Mr. Deville and suddenly receives the career he has always wanted: packed rooms, effortless laughs, money and expensive gifts. When Benny becomes uneasy and tries to end the relationship, Deville reveals that the success was never free. During a drive in a powerful new car whose brakes will not work, Deville identifies himself as the Devil and demands Benny's soul as payment. Benny dies in the crash and awakens in what looks like a miserable old Catskills resort. Deville explains that this is Benny's personal hell, where the comedian is sent back onstage to perform forever for an audience he can never escape.

grh_7855e586b59395995467.title: Colonel Warburton's Madness
paragraphs: Colonel Warburton suffers violent, seemingly insane attacks whenever he hears a mysterious whistle, and dogs that react to the same sound are killed. Holmes demonstrates that a specially made ultrasonic whistle is triggering Warburton's hypersensitive hearing and that the dogs were destroyed because they could expose the trick. grh_786193b00e7ee7b9aebd.title: Lifeline
paragraphs: A dramatization of Robert Carse's Lifeline honors the United States Merchant Marine and the dangerous supply routes that sustained Allied forces. An able seaman describes Arctic convoys, sinkings, lifeboat ordeals and the poor treatment merchant crews sometimes received ashore, then recounts the courage of shipmates carrying men and supplies into combat zones. The closing Guadalcanal episode follows a merchant sailor who volunteers to handle landing craft under fire, is badly wounded getting Marines ashore and dies after completing his job.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.20280ce24fdf32a8|Lifeline]]. Robert Carse is credited as author and Charles Newton adapted it for radio.
